findings.title: Team admin/owner check can never succeed
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. Membership role is a single value, so a user is never both ADMIN and OWNER, and the && short-circuits. If isTeamAdmin matches only ADMIN, the check is always false; if it also treats OWNER as admin, only owners pass and admins still fail. Either way team admins cannot add guests unless they are also the booking organizer or an attendee, which contradicts the variable name and the permission gate. The bookings UI still shows Additional guests on confirmed rows, so those users hit FORBIDDEN. Use ||, and skip the lookup when eventType.teamId is null instead of querying team id 0.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials
findings.body: EventManager is built from the signed-in user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). Calendar BookingReferences are tied to the organizer's credential id (and other hosts' credentials on collective events), not the caller's. The query already loads booking.user with credentials and destinationCalendar and never uses that user. When an attendee adds guests, the host calendar event is not updated. On collective events, other hosts' calendar copies cannot be updated either because only one user's credentials are supplied. Load decrypted credentials for the booking organizer (getUsersCredentials, not the raw Prisma credential rows) and include collective hosts.

findings.title: Any attendee can invite unlimited guests on any booking
findings.body: Authorization only checks organizer, attendee, or the broken team-admin flag. booking.status, end time, and list size are never validated, and ZAddGuestsInputSchema is an unbounded email array. Any logged-in attendee can therefore add as many addresses as they want to a cancelled, rejected, unconfirmed, or past booking. Each new address is sent AttendeeScheduledEmail, and the mailer hardcodes ICS status CONFIRMED. videoCallData (join URL and meeting password) is copied onto the event whenever a video reference exists, so those invites disclose meeting access for events that are not accepted upcoming meetings, and a participant can send unlimited calendar mail through the platform. Restrict this to accepted future bookings and cap the guest list.

findings.title: Seated events are not capacity-checked
findings.body: Guests are inserted as Attendee rows with no comparison to eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot, which is only copied onto the calendar payload later. If occupancy is the attendee count, this overbooks the slot and can block real bookers. If occupancy is BookingSeat / seatsReferences, these guests become attendees with no seat, so seat counts, the seats UI, and cancel/reschedule links diverge from the attendee list. seatsShowAttendees is also ignored: sendAddGuestsEmails and the ICS include every attendee, leaking participant emails on events configured to hide them. Enforce remaining capacity before insert, or reject add-guests for seated events, and honor seatsShowAttendees when emailing.

findings.title: Guests stay saved when calendar or email updates fail
findings.body: prisma.booking.update commits the new Attendee rows before translation loading, updateCalendarAttendees, and sendAddGuestsEmails. The calendar call is outside the try/catch, so a thrown calendar or translation error returns 500 after the insert. A retry then filters those addresses out as already present and throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the calendar update and invite emails are never retried and the user is told the addresses are invalid. Email failures are caught, logged as a static string with the error discarded, and the handler still returns success, so the dialog toasts Guests added when nobody was notified. Roll back or make the side effects retryable, and do not report success when notification failed.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS values are lowercased but not trimmed, and the submitted address is not trimmed or lowercased before includes(). A blocked address with different casing, or a blacklist entry with a leading space after the comma, is stored and emailed. Duplicate detection uses case-sensitive equality, so A@x.com and a@x.com both become Attendee rows, and the organizer's own email is not excluded. The read of existing attendees is also outside a transaction, so two parallel requests can both pass the filter and insert the same guest. Normalize both sides with trim and lowercase, trim blacklist entries, and do not add the organizer as an attendee. Mixed requests currently drop blocked or duplicate addresses silently and still return success.

findings.title: New guests are stored with a blank name
findings.body: Every newly inserted guest is saved with name set to an empty string. Scheduled and add-guest mail payloads address the recipient as `${attendee.name} <${attendee.email}>`, so new guests, who are sent AttendeeScheduledEmail, get a blank display name (` <email>`). The same empty name is sent in the calendar attendee update. Use the email address, or its local part, when no name was collected.

findings.title: Already-invited emails get a new booking confirmation
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw guests input, not uniqueGuests, the addresses actually inserted. In that helper, any attendee whose email is in the list receives AttendeeScheduledEmail (a full new-booking confirmation with cancel and reschedule links) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. If the request includes someone already on the booking plus a new guest, the existing person is not inserted again but still gets a fresh scheduled email and does not get the guests-added notice. The includes() check is also case-sensitive. Pass the normalized list of addresses that were actually added.

findings.title: Add-guest emails ignore disabled standard emails
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer and every attendee. Other helpers in this file (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, sendCancelledEmails, and the rest) skip host or attendee mail when event-type metadata disables standard emails. This helper has no such check, and addGuestsHandler never passes eventType.metadata. Organizers who turned those emails off still get guest-added mail and full AttendeeScheduledEmail messages, including ICS and meeting links, when guests are added. Pass the metadata through and honor the same disable flags.

findings.title: Collective co-hosts are never notified
findings.body: The CalendarEvent built for notifications never sets team or team.members, even though eventType is already loaded. sendAddGuestsEmails only emails extra hosts when calendarEvent.team.members is present, so that loop never runs. On a collective event, only booking.user receives OrganizerAddGuestsEmail; the other hosts are not told that guests were added. Load the event-type hosts and set calEvent.team the same way other booking mail flows do.

findings.title: Add-guests is offered on past bookings
findings.body: The new additional-guests action is added to editBookingActions, which is included in bookedActions. bookedActions is not limited to upcoming meetings: past confirmed bookings and past pending bookings also render TableActions with that list. Using it still inserts attendees and sends AttendeeScheduledEmail plus an ICS REQUEST for a time that already passed. Only show this action for accepted upcoming bookings, and enforce the same rule in addGuestsHandler.

findings.title: No tests for addGuests authorization or failure paths
findings.body: The new mutation ships with no unit or integration tests. The inverted team-admin condition, access to cancelled or past bookings, seated overbooking, blacklist casing, and a calendar or email failure after the attendee insert would not be caught in CI. Cover organizer, team admin, team owner, attendee, and stranger; non-accepted bookings; seat capacity; and a side-effect failure after insert.
